## Interactive viz

The [plotly package](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/plotly/index.html) provides a way of using the [plotly.js library](https://plotly.com/r/) within R

* By creating a plotly object with `plot_ly()`
* By transforming a ggplot object via `ggplotly()`

`ggplotly()` provides a lot of the functionality of `plot_ly()` without learning the details of `plot_ly()`. Because `ggplotly()` returns a `plot_ly()` object, though, it can be modified with additional `plot_ly()` options.

See [Carson Sievert's book](https://plotly-r.com/) for more, especially [Chapter 2](https://plotly-r.com/overview) and [Chapter 33](https://plotly-r.com/improving-ggplotly)!

## plotly::ggplotly() example

```{r plotly, fig.align = "center", fig.width = 10}
cvl_per_workers <- cvl_per %>% 
  filter(!worker_class %in% c("Unemployed", "Not in Labor Force"), 
         wages < 500000) %>% 
  droplevels()

# create median value
med_wage <- cvl_per_workers %>% 
  group_by(worker_class) %>% 
  summarize(samp_total = n(),
            pop_total = sum(pwgtp),
            med_wage = median(wages, na.rm = TRUE))

fig <- cvl_per_workers %>% 
  filter(!is.na(educ_att)) %>% 
  group_by(worker_class, educ_att) %>% 
  summarize(med_wages = median(wages, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = educ_att, y = med_wages, 
             color = worker_class, group = worker_class,
             text = paste("Type of Work: ", worker_class, "<br>",
                          "Educational Attainment: ", educ_att, "<br>",
                          "Median wages: ", med_wages))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Educational Attainment", y = "Median Wages") +
  scale_color_manual(values = 
                       c("#F28E2B", "#E15759", "#4E79A7", "#76B7B2", "#59A14F", "#EDC948"), 
                     guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_currency()) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("No HS\nDeg", "HS\nGrad", "Some\nCollege", 
                              "College\nGrad", "Masters\nDeg", "Doctoral\nDeg")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position='none')

ggplotly(fig, tooltip = c("text")) 
```

## Interactive tables

The [reactable package](https://glin.github.io/reactable/) provides a way of using the React Table JavaScript library within R

* Has interactive functionality (sorting, filtering) like DT::datatable()
* With more formatting and conditionaly styling like kableExtra

With additional and simplified formatting and customization provided in the [reactablefmtr package](https://kcuilla.github.io/reactablefmtr/).

## reactable::reactable() example

```{r reactable}
# base table
industry_table <- cvl_per %>% 
  filter(!is.na(ind_group), ind_group != "no_work") %>% 
  group_by(ind_group) %>% 
  summarize(employees = sum(pwgtp),
            med_wages = median(wages, na.rm = TRUE),
            med_hours = median(wkhp, na.rm = TRUE),
            prop_college = sum(schl_num > 20)/employees,
            prop_private = sum(worker_class == "Private Sector")/employees)

reactable(industry_table,
          columns = list(
            ind_group = colDef(name = "Industry"),
            employees = colDef(name = "Employees"),
            med_wages = colDef(name = "Median Wages",
                               format = colFormat(prefix = "$", separators = TRUE)),
            med_hours = colDef(name = "Hours/ Week"),
            prop_college = colDef(name = "% College Degree",
                                  format = colFormat(percent = TRUE, digits = 1),
                                  style = color_scales(industry_table, 
                                                       colors = rcartocolor::carto_pal(n = 4, "TealRose"))),
            prop_private = colDef(name = "% Private Sector",
                                  format = colFormat(percent = TRUE, digits = 1),
                                  cell = data_bars(industry_table,
                                                   number_fmt = scales::percent_format(scale = 100),
                                                   fill_color = rcartocolor::carto_pal(n = 5, "TealRose")[3]))),
          showSortable = TRUE, filterable = TRUE, defaultPageSize = 5)
```

## Interactive maps

The [leaflet package](https://rstudio.github.io/leaflet/) provides an interface to the Leaflet JavaScript library within R. The leaflet package supports

* features like panning and zooming
* multiple elements like markers, polygons, lines, and popups
* layered on base map tiles from open street map, cartoDB, esri and [other providers](https://leaflet-extras.github.io/leaflet-providers/preview/) (often with registration)

Other interactive map libraries: tmap, mapview, mapdeck

## leaflet::leaflet() example
```{r map, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6}
# create a palette function
pal <- colorNumeric(carto_pal(7, "Sunset"), 
                    reverse = FALSE, 
                    domain = rent_own_va$prop_renting*100) 

leaflet() %>% 
  addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") %>% 
  addPolygons(data = rent_own_va,
              fillColor = ~pal(prop_renting*100),
              fillOpacity = 0.8,
              weight = 2, 
              opacity = 1,
              color = "white",
              highlight = highlightOptions(
                weight = 3,
                fillOpacity = 0.9,
                bringToFront = T),
              popup = paste0("Locality: ", rent_own_va$county, "<br>",
                             "% Renting: ", round(rent_own_va$prop_renting*100, 1))) %>% 
  addLegend("topleft", pal = pal, values = rent_own_va$prop_renting*100, 
            title = "% Renting", opacity = 0.7)
```
